- `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400 `display is required when showBrowser=true (no DISPLAY detected)` — `showBrowser=true` with no `display` field on `GET /api/v1/browser/start` and no `$DISPLAY` env.
- `TIMEOUT` 408 / 504 — the request passed the kit's request deadline (600 s by default). While the request is launching or restarting the instance this is a 504 with `details.phase: "launch"` and `details.outcome: "unknown"`: the instance may still come up, so check `GET /api/v1/browser/metadata` with `start=false` before retrying. After the request was forwarded to a running instance it is a 504 with `details.phase: "proxy"` and `details.outcome: "unknown"`: the call may already have taken effect (a `POST /api/v1/browser/viewport` included), so inspect the state before repeating a mutation. A request that times out while its body is still arriving is a 408. Any other work the kit does itself (a long `GET /api/v1/browser/history` query, an `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` waiting for the start of the same instance) is a 504 with `details.phase: "server"` and `details.outcome: "unknown"`: the work is not cancelled and may still complete, so inspect the state before repeating a mutation.
- `TIMEOUT` 504 — an automation call (`GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot`, `POST /api/v1/browser/action`, `POST /api/v1/browser/wait`) spent its `timeoutMs` budget (default 10000, max 30000). `details.phase` says where; `details.outcome` `not-started` means the action was never dispatched. For `POST /api/v1/browser/wait` this is how a condition that never held is reported.
- `STALE_SNAPSHOT` 409 — the ref's snapshot is no longer the tab's latest, or the main frame navigated; take a new snapshot. When `details.outcome` is present, read it before repeating an action (see Quirks).
- `INSTANCE_CHANGED` 409 — the `instanceGeneration` sent no longer matches the running instance (`details.expected` is null when no instance exists); re-read `GET /api/v1/browser/metadata`.
- `TAB_BUSY` 409 — another gated operation is in flight on that tab (`POST /api/v1/browser/action`, `GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot`, `POST /api/v1/browser/browse`, `POST /api/v1/browser/tab/close`, or a screenshot, PDF or markdown call that carries a `url`); `details.op` names it; wait for it. `POST /api/v1/browser/wait` never takes the gate.
- `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET` 409 — the target matched more than one element; narrow it or use a ref.
- `TAB_NOT_FOUND` 404 — no tab with that `tabId`; `details.openTabs` lists the open ones.
- `INSTANCE_QUARANTINED` 502 — the slot's previous browser process has not been confirmed exited, so no new instance can start there yet; retry later.
- `SHUTTING_DOWN` 503 — the kit is shutting down.
- `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` 405 — only GET/POST/DELETE/PUT/PATCH.

## Related namespaces

- `display` — headful renders into `display-{n}`; the `?view=display` page iframes it.
- `terminal` — helper CLIs.
- `curl` — JS-free HTTP.
- `files` — pull artefacts out.
- `sqlite` — persist scraped data.
- `exec` — server post-processing.

## Examples

Each step has a copy-pasteable code block in the mode you're reading (curl for HTTP, `hoody` for CLI, TypeScript for SDK). Set `P`, `C`, `N` (project id, computer id, server name) from `GET /api/v1/computers/{id}` first. Warning: The `browser-X` hostname selects the instance; the proxy overwrites a `browser_port` or `display` in the query, and a `browser_id` (or a `browser_port`/`display` in a JSON body) that names another instance is refused with 400 `INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT` (see the Quirks gotcha). Examples 1–5 and 8–9 use slot 1 (`browser-1`); Examples 6 and 7 use slots 2 and 3 so their different launch options do not collide with slot 1's running instance.

### 1. Spin up a headless instance and navigate to a URL

**Goal:** boot a Chromium instance, point it at a page, confirm it's alive. Headless avoids the X-display dependency (`showBrowser=false`).

**Step 1 — start.** Returns the start-response payload (`engine`, `headless`, `chromiumBuildId`, `browser_host`, `browser_port`). `GET /api/v1/browser/start` is idempotent — calling it again on the same slot returns the existing instance and ignores new options (a different `stealth` value is rejected with `409`).

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
curl -sf "$KIT/start?showBrowser=false&stealth=false" \
  | jq '{engine,headless,chromiumBuildId,browser_port}'
```

**Step 2 — navigate.** `POST /api/v1/browser/browse` opens or reuses a tab and waits for load.

```bash
curl -sf -X POST "$KIT/browse" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://httpbin.org/html"}' | jq '.'
```

### 2. Full-page PNG screenshot

**Goal:** capture the entire scrolled height (not just the viewport). `format=base64` returns `{ data: "<b64>" }`; the default `format=png` returns raw `image/png` bytes.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
# Raw PNG bytes:
curl -sf "$KIT/screenshot?fullPage=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhttpbin.org%2Fhtml" \
  -o /tmp/page.png
file /tmp/page.png
# Or base64-wrapped:
curl -sf "$KIT/screenshot?fullPage=true&format=base64" | jq -r .data | head -c 80
```

### 3. Get the page HTML and the rendered text

**Goal:** read the post-JS DOM (HTML) and the page text. `GET /api/v1/browser/text` returns `body.innerText` when the document has a body. Without one, such as in an XML or SVG document, it returns the root element's text content, or an empty string if there is no root element.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
curl -sf "$KIT/html"  | head -c 200
echo
curl -sf "$KIT/text"  | head -c 200
```

### 4. Execute JavaScript in the page and capture the return value

**Goal:** run a script in the page context. Over HTTP, `GET /api/v1/browser/eval?script=` puts the script in the query (size-bound by URL). `POST /api/v1/browser/eval` accepts `{ script }` JSON via the SDK / CLI / `Content-Type: application/json`; raw `Content-Type: text/plain` HTTP also works (body = script source). Either shape returns `{ result }` (`{}` when the script returns nothing). The script reads the DOM on every engine; page JS globals (`window.__NEXT_DATA__`, app stores) are visible when the reported engine is `playwright` (including after a fallback), and read as `undefined` when it is `patchright` (see Quirks).

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
# GET — small expression:
curl -sf "$KIT/eval?script=$(python3 -c 'import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote("document.title"))')"
echo
# POST — JSON body:
curl -sf -X POST "$KIT/eval" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"script":"JSON.stringify({title: document.title, links: document.querySelectorAll(\"a\").length})"}'
```

### 5. Set cookies and read them back

**Goal:** prime the cookie jar, then verify. POST body is a JSON object `{ cookies: [...] }` whose entries need `name`, `value`, and either an absolute http(s) `url` or both `domain` and `path`; do not combine `url` with `domain` or `path` (400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field). Optional: `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite` (`Strict|Lax|None`), `expires` (Unix seconds, -1 = session).

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
curl -sf -X POST "$KIT/cookies" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"cookies":[
        {"name":"session","value":"abc123","url":"https://httpbin.org"},
        {"name":"theme","value":"dark","url":"https://httpbin.org"}
      ]}' | jq .
# → {"added": 2}
curl -sf "$KIT/cookies?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhttpbin.org" | jq .
```

### 6. Authenticated scrape — set session cookie, browse, extract, clear

**Goal:** scrape a logged-in page without re-doing OAuth. Pre-load the session cookie a real login would have set, hit the protected URL, read text, then DELETE the jar.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-2.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"   # slot 2
curl -sf "$KIT/start?showBrowser=false&stealth=false" >/dev/null
curl -sf -X POST "$KIT/cookies" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"cookies":[{"name":"sessionid","value":"REAL_TOKEN","url":"https://app.example.com"}]}'
curl -sf "$KIT/browse?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com%2Fdashboard"
curl -sf "$KIT/text"   | head -c 400
curl -sX DELETE "$KIT/cookies"   # → {"cleared": true}
```

### 7. `POST /api/v1/browser/browse` with explicit viewport, locale, and User-Agent

**Goal:** mimic a French mobile Safari to test geo/UA-gated content. Browser-context settings (`viewport`, `locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgent`) apply when `GET /api/v1/browser/start` creates a new instance: on a slot that already has one, `start` returns that instance with its existing settings (or answers 409 `INSTANCE_BACKEND_MISMATCH` when `stealth` or `browser` differs), so stop it first to relaunch with these. `POST /api/v1/browser/browse` carries the navigation body.

`viewport` is a JSON string such as `'{"width":390,"height":844}'`. `geolocation` is a JSON string such as `'{"latitude":48.8566,"longitude":2.3522,"accuracy":20}'`.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-3.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"   # slot 3
curl -sf "$KIT/start?showBrowser=false&stealth=true\
&viewport=%7B%22width%22%3A390%2C%22height%22%3A844%7D\
&locale=fr-FR\
&timezoneId=Europe%2FParis\
&userAgent=Mozilla%2F5.0%20(iPhone%3B%20CPU%20iPhone%20OS%2017_4%20like%20Mac%20OS%20X)%20AppleWebKit%2F605.1.15%20(KHTML%2C%20like%20Gecko)%20Version%2F17.4%20Mobile%2F15E148%20Safari%2F604.1\
&geolocation=%7B%22latitude%22%3A48.8566%2C%22longitude%22%3A2.3522%2C%22accuracy%22%3A20%7D" >/dev/null
curl -sf -X POST "$KIT/browse" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://httpbin.org/headers","active":true,"onlyIfNotExists":false}'
curl -sf "$KIT/text" | head -c 500
```

### 8. Inspect browsing history (filter by domain, then delete older entries)

**Goal:** When history is enabled, the kit records browser navigations under `/hoody/storage/hoody-browser/history` by default, but recording is not guaranteed. The page-navigation listener skips `about:blank`; API-triggered navigations are recorded through a separate path. Retention defaults to 30 days and is configurable, as is the directory. A query returns at most 500 entries per page. The delete step has no domain filter: it removes every entry older than the cutoff on the selected slot, for all domains. Query (through a `browser-N` host, slot N's entries only), then selectively delete.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
# Slot 1's navs in the last hour, max 50:
SINCE=$(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%FT%TZ)
curl -sf "$KIT/history?since=$SINCE&limit=50" | jq '{total, has_more, sample: .entries[0]}'
# Just one domain:
curl -sf "$KIT/history?domain=httpbin.org&limit=20" | jq '.entries | length'
# Drop entries older than 7 days recorded on slot 1, for every domain:
BEFORE=$(date -u -d '7 days ago' +%FT%TZ)
curl -sX DELETE "$KIT/history?before=$BEFORE&browser_id=1" | jq .
# → {"deleted": <n>}
```

### 9. Capture instance metadata (engine, viewport, debug URL)

**Goal:** introspect what the kit actually launched — engine (`playwright`/`patchright`), Chromium build, executable path, current display, debug socket. Use `start=false` to query *without* auto-starting (404 if no instance exists).

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser"
curl -sf "$KIT/metadata?start=false" \
  | jq '{engine, stealth, headless, chromiumBuildId, browser_host, browser_port, fingerprintId, display, iframe_url}'
# Live tabs in the instance:
curl -sf "$KIT/tabs?start=false" | jq '.'
```

For an external CDP attachment, `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` returns the live `webSocketDebuggerUrl` (CDP is on by default; default `useRemoteDebuggingPort=true`). If you started with `useRemoteDebuggingPort=false`, the call still returns 200 but `webSocketDebuggerUrl` is null. A 404 `Instance not found` means no instance exists at all (this route never starts an instance and ignores `start`).

### 10. Stop and shutdown — the ONLY safe ending

**Goal:** browser instances stay alive across requests until they are stopped or the kit process restarts (graceful kit restart SIGTERMs every child — see Quirks & gotchas). The idle sweep reaps an instance nobody has used for the max age (1 h by default), so a forgotten instance is eventually reclaimed, and one you still need must see a request at least once per idle window. Each slot has a fixed port, so a slot whose previous process has not been confirmed exited answers `502 INSTANCE_QUARANTINED` until it has; retry later rather than restarting the computer.

`GET /api/v1/browser/stop` and `GET /api/v1/browser/shutdown` both end the child, and its SIGTERM handler deletes its profile dir (the same cleanup as `/shutdown`). Every Chromium instance runs on a persistent profile of its own, with or without extensions (an extension profile under the kit's browser data dir, otherwise under the temp dir), and a new instance never reuses one, so cookies and logins do not carry over to the next instance. Profile cleanup is best-effort: a child killed before it cleans up (SIGKILL, OOM) leaves its profile until the stale-profile sweep that runs when a later instance starts; that sweep removes only profiles provably stale (a profile with no owner record, or an unreadable one, is kept), so a killed child that wrote its record is normally swept on a later start. One `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` per instance is a complete teardown — calling both is redundant.

```bash
for X in 1 2 3; do
  curl -sX GET "https://${P}-${C}-browser-${X}.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser/stop" | jq .
done
# /shutdown never creates an instance either (404 on an empty slot); start=false is unnecessary.
# Count what is still registered (a quarantined slot is not counted):
curl -sf "https://${P}-${C}-browser-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/api/v1/browser/metrics" | jq '.instances.total'
```

A `404 Instance not found` from `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` means no instance is registered on that slot: it is gone, or it is quarantined after an exit that was not confirmed. Neither `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` nor `GET /api/v1/browser/shutdown` creates an instance: on an empty slot both answer `404 Instance not found`. `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` waits a bounded time for the child to exit before it answers, and answers 200 even when that exit is not confirmed: the slot is then quarantined and answers `502 INSTANCE_QUARANTINED` until the process exits; `GET /api/v1/browser/shutdown` answers 200 as soon as shutdown starts and finishes in the background. The instance leaves routing before the reply, so `GET /api/v1/browser/metadata` with `start=false` answers 404 at once and does not show that the process exited. To wait for the teardown, call `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` on the same slot: it waits for the shutdown in flight to settle, then answers `404 Instance not found`. A later `GET /api/v1/browser/start` answers `502 INSTANCE_QUARANTINED` if the exit was not confirmed. Use `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` alone when you need the bounded wait.

## Reference

**Param notes for every section** (a parameter named here means this wherever a row lists it, unless its own section says otherwise):

- `browser_id` — Selects the instance: SDK and CLI clients send the request to the `browser-<N>` service host. A value that conflicts with the host's instance is refused with 400 INSTANCE_SELECTOR_CONFLICT. On `/history` it also filters. Against a bare server it selects nothing; address instances there with `browser_host` + `browser_port`.
- `start` — Controls instance creation behavior. Default mode: instances are created automatically. Set to `false` to prevent creation. When auto-start is disabled globally: set to `true` to create an instance. Three states, all distinct: omitted means "create one if this deployment creates instances automatically", `false` means "never create one", and `true` means "create one even where automatic creation is turned off". Because omitting it is NOT equivalent to sending `true`, this parameter deliberately declares no schema default: do not add one, and do not let a client materialise schema defaults into the request, or every call silently becomes an explicit `true`. `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` is the exception: it answers 404 when no instance is running and never consults this value.

### `cookies` (3) — Cookie management

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `DELETE /api/v1/browser/cookies` | Clear all cookies | `?browser_id` `?start` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/cookies` | Get cookies | `?browser_id` `?start` `?url` |
| `POST /api/v1/browser/cookies` | Set cookies | `?browser_id` `?start` `body*` |

**Param notes:**

- `url` — Filter cookies by URL. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`): the server's rule is on the key, not on the operation, so it applies here too even though this parameter is declared inline rather than shared.

**Body shapes:**

- `POST /api/v1/browser/cookies` body — `{ cookies*: { name*: string, value*: string, url: string, domain: string, path: string, expires: number, httpOnly: bool, secure: bool, sameSite: "Strict" | "Lax" | "None" }[] }`

### `history` (2) — Browsing history

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `DELETE /api/v1/browser/history` | Delete browsing history | `?before` `?browser_id` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/history` | Query browsing history | `?since` `?domain` `?browser_id` `?limit` `?offset` |

**Param notes:**

- `before` — Delete entries before this ISO 8601 timestamp
- `browser_id` — Delete entries for specific browser ID only. Through a `browser-{N}` service hostname it may only be `N` (the default there). _(on `DELETE /api/v1/browser/history`)_
- `since` — Return entries after this ISO 8601 timestamp
- `domain` — Filter by domain (exact match)
- `browser_id` — Filter by browser ID. Through a `browser-{N}` service hostname it may only be `N` (the default there). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/history`)_
- `limit` — Maximum entries to return (1-500)
- `offset` — Number of entries to skip for pagination

### `instances` (6) — Operations for inspecting and controlling browser instances

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/v1/browser/metadata` | Get instance metadata | `?browser_id` `?start` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/devtools-url` | Get DevTools URLs | `?browser_id` `?start` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/restart` | Restart browser instance | `?browser_id` `?start` `?chromiumVersion` `?fingerprintId` `?useRemoteDebuggingPort` `?remoteDebuggingPort` `?remoteDebuggingAddress` `?extensions` `?extensionsDir` `?extensionsStoreIds` `?proxyServer` `?proxyUsername` `?proxyPassword` `?proxyBypass` `?enableQuic` `?enableDnsOverHttps` `?dnsOverHttpsUrl` `?display` `?showBrowser` `?sessionName` `?timezoneId` `?locale` `?userAgent` `?viewport` `?noViewport` `?geolocation` `?launchArguments` `?browser` `?firefoxVersion` `?firefoxExecutablePath` `?showDevtools` `?userProfile` `?stealth` `?iframe` `?iframe_url` `?maximize_new_windows` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/shutdown` | Shutdown browser instance | `?browser_id` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/start` | Create or retrieve browser instance | `?browser_id` `?chromiumVersion` `?fingerprintId` `?useRemoteDebuggingPort` `?remoteDebuggingPort` `?remoteDebuggingAddress` `?extensions` `?extensionsDir` `?extensionsStoreIds` `?proxyServer` `?proxyUsername` `?proxyPassword` `?proxyBypass` `?enableQuic` `?enableDnsOverHttps` `?dnsOverHttpsUrl` `?display` `?showBrowser` `?sessionName` `?timezoneId` `?locale` `?userAgent` `?viewport` `?noViewport` `?geolocation` `?launchArguments` `?browser` `?firefoxVersion` `?firefoxExecutablePath` `?showDevtools` `?userProfile` `?stealth` `?iframe` `?iframe_url` `?maximize_new_windows` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/stop` | Stop browser instance | `?browser_id` |

**Param notes:**

- `chromiumVersion` — Chromium/Chrome version selection for the instance. This option applies only when `browser=chromium`. Supported formats: Full version: `136.0.7103.113`; Major version: `136` (mapped to a known stable patch for the current OS); Channel tag: `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary` Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `chromiumVersion`. A full version that no download source has is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too, answered once the download is refused. A major version with no known build is treated as if omitted. Omitted, the server uses the Chrome major of a `userAgent` you pass, and otherwise the Chrome build supplied with the computer: the stable build from its last successful update, so it starts without a download. It may lag the newest stable, and `browserFullVersion` in the metadata reports the version that started. If the computer has no supplied build, the server resolves the current `stable` build. Pass `stable` (or a version) to resolve it when the instance starts; a build the computer does not have is downloaded on first use. The request **blocks** until the requested browser build is available on the server.
- `fingerprintId` — Base fingerprint profile id. The server uses the `context` and `launch` defaults of the configured fingerprint profile with this id, then applies any request overrides over them (top-level options and `userProfile` values both win over the profile). An unknown id starts with an empty profile. The id is 1-64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`; any other value is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- `useRemoteDebuggingPort` — If `true`, the instance will launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port` and will populate `webSocketDebuggerUrl` in metadata responses. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `remoteDebuggingPort` — Ignored. The kit always assigns the DevTools port itself (a caller-supplied value is never honoured, for isolation); read the assigned URLs from `/devtools-url` or the instance metadata. Kept only so older clients do not fail validation.
- `remoteDebuggingAddress` — Interface address the DevTools port binds to. Connect through the URLs `/devtools-url` returns.
- `extensions` — Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of absolute extension directory paths to load. Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.
- `extensionsDir` — Directory containing extension subfolders to load (each subfolder is treated as an extension). Extensions are Chromium only (`browser=chromium`, the default; with Firefox the start fails) and require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode); they launch a persistent profile.
- `extensionsStoreIds` — Chrome Web Store extension IDs to download and load (Chromium only). Requires `showBrowser=true` and works only with `browser=chromium`. Each ID is 32 letters from `a` to `p`; anything else, or an ID the store does not offer, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Downloads of the same extension are serialized across instances; an instance that waits more than 5 minutes for another instance's download fails with a "try again later" error. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `proxyServer` — Proxy server URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h) _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `proxyUsername` — Proxy username (if required). Only with an `http://` or `https://` `proxyServer`: the browser cannot authenticate to a SOCKS proxy, so `proxyUsername` or `proxyPassword` with a `socks4://` or `socks5://` proxy (and `socks5h://` under Firefox) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- `proxyPassword` — Proxy password (if required)
- `proxyBypass` — Comma-separated list of hosts that should bypass the proxy
- `enableQuic` — Enable QUIC/HTTP3 transport (`false` blocks QUIC). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `enableDnsOverHttps` — Enable DNS-over-HTTPS for browser DNS resolution. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `dnsOverHttpsUrl` — DoH resolver URL (HTTPS only). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `display` — X display number or identifier for headful mode. Required when `showBrowser=true` and no `DISPLAY` environment variable is set on the server.
- `showBrowser` — Whether to run the browser headful (visible). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `sessionName` — Custom session name for identifying this browser instance
- `timezoneId` — IANA timezone identifier for browser geolocation
- `locale` — BCP 47 language tag for browser locale
- `userAgent` — User agent string to apply to the browser context.
- `viewport` — Viewport configuration as JSON string. Example: {"width":1920,"height":1080,"deviceScaleFactor":1} Pass `null` to disable fixed-viewport emulation entirely: the page then follows the real browser window size (responsive; most useful in headful mode).
- `noViewport` — Set to `true` to disable fixed-viewport emulation (alias for `viewport=null`). The page then resizes with the browser window instead of being pinned to an emulated resolution. Cannot be combined with a fixed `viewport` object. On a restart, `false` turns off a `noViewport=true` the instance was started with, and the default viewport comes back. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `geolocation` — Geolocation configuration as JSON string. Example: {"latitude":40.7128,"longitude":-74.0060,"accuracy":100} Anything other than a JSON object (`null`, an array, a number) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, and so is an object without both `latitude` and `longitude` or with a negative `accuracy` (meters).
- `launchArguments` — Additional Chromium/Firefox command-line arguments. Pass the query key repeatedly (`launchArguments=--a&launchArguments=--b`) or a single JSON array string (`launchArguments=["--a","--b"]`); every value is kept. Entries must be strings (400 otherwise). On Chromium, every entry must be a switch (`--name` or `--name=value`) that does not open a page: a positional URL or path and `--app` are refused, because a startup page loads before the browser's local-file block is in place. A kit started with local-file access enabled accepts them.
- `browser` — Browser engine (`chromium` or `firefox`). The raw HTTP query also accepts `chrome` as an alias of `chromium`; the SDK and the CLI accept only `chromium` and `firefox`. Fixed for the life of the instance: when omitted, the instance keeps its engine. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `firefoxVersion` — Firefox version label (informational only). Playwright-managed Firefox builds are used by default. If omitted, a Playwright Firefox build is downloaded on demand. A value that is not a label (letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`, at most 64 characters) is ignored.
- `firefoxExecutablePath` — Absolute path to a custom Firefox executable (overrides download)
- `showDevtools` — Whether to open DevTools on launch (Chromium only). When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `userProfile` — Optional user profile object (JSON string): `locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgentString`, `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport`. Precedence for each field: the top-level request option (`locale`, `timezoneId`, `userAgent`, `geolocation`, `viewport`) > `userProfile` > the fingerprint profile (`fingerprintId`, `default` when omitted) > the engine default. A value set here always replaces the fingerprint profile's value. `geolocation` and `deviceProfile.viewport` must be objects and get the same checks as the top-level `geolocation` and `viewport`; a bad value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the field. An empty value (`null`, `false`, `0`, `""`) is treated as not set.
- `stealth` — Launch Chromium in stealth mode using Patchright (anti-detection patches). Only applies to `browser=chromium`. Ignored for Firefox. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. Bare `?stealth` is treated as `true`. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `iframe` — The bare `/` URL serves the instance status page. Open `/?view=display` for the full-page display; if no display address can be resolved, the status page is returned. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `iframe_url` — Explicit URL for the display iframe. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `maximize_new_windows` — Control the `maximize_new_windows` flag stamped onto the generated display URL (always explicit `true`/`false`); when true the hoody-display client opens new top-level app windows maximized. When omitted, the instance keeps its setting. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/restart`)_
- `useRemoteDebuggingPort` — If `true`, the instance will launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port` and will populate `webSocketDebuggerUrl` in metadata responses. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `extensionsStoreIds` — Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of Chrome Web Store extension IDs to download and load. Requires `showBrowser=true` and works only with `browser=chromium`. Each ID is 32 letters from `a` to `p`; anything else, or an ID the store does not offer, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Downloads of the same extension are serialized across instances; an instance that waits more than 5 minutes for another instance's download fails with a "try again later" error. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `proxyServer` — Proxy server for browser traffic. Supports `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, or `socks5h://`. Example: `socks5://127.0.0.1:9050` _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `enableQuic` — Enable QUIC/HTTP3 transport. Defaults to `false` (QUIC blocked). Use `enableQuic=true` to re-enable QUIC. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `enableDnsOverHttps` — Enable DNS-over-HTTPS for browser DNS resolution. Defaults to `true`. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `dnsOverHttpsUrl` — DoH resolver URL (HTTPS only). Defaults to Cloudflare: `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query`. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `showBrowser` — Whether to run the browser headful (visible). Defaults to `true`. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `noViewport` — Set to `true` to disable fixed-viewport emulation (alias for `viewport=null`). The page then resizes with the browser window instead of being pinned to an emulated resolution. Cannot be combined with a fixed `viewport` object. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `browser` — Browser engine to use (`chromium` or `firefox`). The raw HTTP query also accepts `chrome` as an alias of `chromium`; the SDK and the CLI accept only `chromium` and `firefox`. Fixed for the life of the instance. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `showDevtools` — Whether to open DevTools on launch (Chromium only) _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `stealth` — Launch Chromium in stealth mode using Patchright (anti-detection patches). Only applies to `browser=chromium`. Ignored for Firefox. Defaults to `true`. Bare `?stealth` is treated as `true`. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `iframe` — The bare `/` URL serves the instance status page. Open `/?view=display` for the full-page display; if no display address can be resolved, the status page is returned. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `iframe_url` — Explicit URL for the display iframe. If not provided, the URL is auto-detected from the Host header subdomain pattern. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_
- `maximize_new_windows` — Control the `maximize_new_windows` flag stamped onto generated display URLs (iframe pages, status pages, `iframe_url` metadata). The flag is always explicit (`true` or `false`); when true the hoody-display client opens new top-level app windows maximized. Enabled by default; set to `false` to keep the display client's centered default-size placement (the explicit `false` also overrides a display-side `default-settings.txt` enable). Explicit `iframe_url` values are never modified. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/start`)_

### `kit` (2) — Server monitoring and health check operations

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/v1/browser/health` | Health check |  |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/metrics` | Server metrics |  |

### `logs` (2) — Console and network logs

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/v1/browser/console` | Get console logs | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` `?type` `?since` `?clear` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/network` | Get network logs | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` `?since` `?clear` |

**Param notes:**

- `tabId` — The ID of an open tab, from `/tabs`; tab ids start at 1. Omitted: all tabs for `/console` and `/network`; a new tab for `/browse`, unless `onlyIfNotExists=true` finds a tab already showing the URL; the active tab for other tab operations. Supplied: exactly that tab. An unknown id returns `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND` (with `details.openTabs`) and a malformed id `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; the request never falls back to another tab. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`tabId must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.
- `type` — Filter by message type (log, error, warning, info, etc.). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`type must not be repeated`).
- `since` — Only return entries at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time, like `2026-10-05T12:00:00Z`. Omitted or empty means no time filter. Any other value (an epoch number, a word like `yesterday`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `since`, never an unfiltered list. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`since must not be repeated`).
- `clear` — Clear the buffer after reading. `true` clears it; `false`, an empty value or omitting it leaves it. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `clear`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`clear must not be repeated`).

### `page` (12) — Operations for interacting with browser tabs and content

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `POST /api/v1/browser/action` | Perform a native element action | `?browser_id` `body*` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/screenshot` | Capture browser screenshot | `?browser_id` `?start` `?url` `?tabId` `?format` `?quality` `?fullPage` `?selector` `?clip` `?mask` `?maskColor` `?hide` `?scale` |
| `POST /api/v1/browser/eval` | Execute JavaScript (POST) | `?browser_id` `?start` `body*:application/json,text/plain` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/eval` | Execute JavaScript | `?browser_id` `?start` `?tabId` `?timeoutMs` `?scriptBase64` `?script*` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/pdf` | Export page as PDF | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` `?url` `?format` `?landscape` `?printBackground` `?margin` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/html` | Get page HTML | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/markdown` | Get page as Markdown | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` `?url` `?onlyMainContent` `?includeImages` `?includeLinks` `?frontmatter` `?maxChars` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot` | Accessibility snapshot of a tab with element refs | `?browser_id` `?instanceGeneration` `?tabId` `?timeoutMs` `?maxChars` `?includeValues` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/text` | Get page text | `?browser_id` `?tabId` `?start` |
| `POST /api/v1/browser/browse` | Navigate to URL (POST) | `?browser_id` `?start` `body*` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/browse` | Navigate to URL | `?browser_id` `?start` `?url` `?tabId` `?waitUntil` `?timeoutMs` `?instanceGeneration` `?active` `?onlyIfNotExists` `?ignoreGetParameters` |
| `POST /api/v1/browser/wait` | Wait for a condition in a tab | `?browser_id` `body*` |

**Param notes:**

- `url` — The URL to navigate to. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: a request naming two destinations is answered rather than silently resolved to one of them. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `url` is governed by the body schema. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). Every other `about:` page is refused (Firefox's `about:reader?url=file:…` loads a local file), and `chrome:` is refused on Firefox, where it is the browser's own privileged UI. A value that is not a string is `url must be a string`. The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On `/screenshot` and `/pdf` a supplied but empty `url=` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too (omit `url` to capture the current tab). The browser itself blocks local files as well (see "Local files" in the API overview). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/screenshot`, `GET /api/v1/browser/browse`)_
- `tabId` — The ID of an open tab, from `/tabs`; tab ids start at 1. Omitted: all tabs for `/console` and `/network`; a new tab for `/browse`, unless `onlyIfNotExists=true` finds a tab already showing the URL; the active tab for other tab operations. Supplied: exactly that tab. An unknown id returns `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND` (with `details.openTabs`) and a malformed id `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; the request never falls back to another tab. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`tabId must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.
- `format` — Output format: `png` (default) and `jpeg` answer the image bytes; `base64` answers JSON with the PNG bytes base64-encoded. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `format`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`format must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/screenshot`)_
- `quality` — Image quality for JPEG format (0-100); not used for `png` or `base64`. A value that is not an integer from 0 to 100 is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `quality`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`quality must not be repeated`).
- `fullPage` — Capture the entire scrollable page. `true` or `false`; any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `fullPage`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`fullPage must not be repeated`).
- `selector` — Capture only the first element matching this CSS selector, at its own size; the page is scrolled to bring it into view. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`selector=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `selector`. No match is `404 ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND`, and a match that is not visible (hidden, or with no size) or that `hide` covers (itself or anything it is rendered inside: an ancestor, a slot, a shadow host) is `422 ELEMENT_NOT_VISIBLE`, both at once rather than after the capture timeout. Cannot be combined with `clip` or `fullPage=true` (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`selector must not be repeated`).
- `clip` — Capture one area: `x,y,width,height` in CSS pixels from the page's top-left corner, for example `0,0,800,600`. `x` and `y` from 0 to 1000000, `width` and `height` above 0 and at most 16384; an empty `clip=` is refused too. With `fullPage=true` the area is measured on the whole page, otherwise on the viewport, and it is cut to what is there; an area entirely outside is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `clip`, and so is a malformed value. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`clip must not be repeated`).
- `mask` — Paint over every element matching this CSS selector with an opaque box in `maskColor`: in the top page and its open shadow roots, not inside iframes. A selector list such as `.cookie-banner, .ad` covers several. This is the option for keeping private data out of an image. A selector that matches nothing covers nothing and the capture still succeeds, so check it against the page first (for example with /snapshot) when the cover matters. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`mask=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `mask`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`mask must not be repeated`).
- `maskColor` — The colour of the `mask` boxes, as an opaque hex colour: `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` (a colour with alpha, which would let the covered content show through, is refused). Default `#FF00FF` (pink). Any other value, an empty one, or `maskColor` without `mask`, is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `maskColor`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`maskColor must not be repeated`).
- `hide` — Leave out every element matching this CSS selector: a style rule (`visibility: hidden; opacity: 0`, both `!important`) is added to the page, every iframe and every open shadow root for the capture only and removed after it, so matches keep their space and are not painted, children included (except a child that sets `visibility: visible` inside a `display: contents` match, which has no box of its own to fade). It is a style rule, not a cover: a declaration the page itself marks `!important` in an element's `style` attribute wins over it, and a selector that matches nothing hides nothing while the capture still succeeds. To keep private data out of an image, use `mask`. One CSS selector, at most 4096 characters (a selector list such as `.a, .b` is one). `>>` chaining, braces, comments, Playwright's own pseudo-classes (`:visible`, `:has-text()`, `:text()` and the like, also escaped; the same text inside a quoted value or an escaped name is fine), an empty value (`hide=`; omit the key instead), and a selector that the page's CSS parser or the engine's selector parser does not accept are each a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `hide`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`hide must not be repeated`).
- `scale` — `device` (default, also when `scale` is empty): one image pixel per device pixel, so a page with `devicePixelRatio` 2 gives an image twice its CSS size. `css`: one image pixel per CSS pixel. Any other non-empty value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `scale`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`scale must not be repeated`).
- `timeoutMs` — Time limit for the script, in milliseconds (1 to 30000, default 30000). When it is spent the kit stops the script and answers `504 TIMEOUT` (`details.phase` `evaluate`); `details.terminated: false` means the script could not be stopped and may still be running, so check the tab before repeating a script with side effects. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`timeoutMs must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/eval`)_
- `scriptBase64` — Set to `true` when `script` is base64-encoded (a `base64:` prefix on the script is also accepted). Avoids URL-encoding issues for scripts with special characters. `true` or `false`; any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `scriptBase64`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`scriptBase64 must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema.
- `script` — JavaScript code to execute (can be base64 encoded). Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`script must not be repeated`): two copies are two different programs and only the last would run. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `script` is governed by the body schema.
- `url` — Optional URL to navigate to before generating the PDF. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). Every other `about:` page is refused (Firefox's `about:reader?url=file:…` loads a local file), and `chrome:` is refused on Firefox, where it is the browser's own privileged UI. A value that is not a string is `url must be a string`. The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, created or reused, or anything is navigated, and before `/pdf`'s `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. On `/screenshot` and `/pdf` a supplied but empty `url=` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` too (omit `url` to capture the current tab). The browser itself blocks local files as well (see "Local files" in the API overview). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`): the server's rule is on the key, not on the operation, so it applies here too even though this parameter is declared inline rather than shared. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/pdf`)_
- `format` — Paper format: one of Letter, Legal, Tabloid, Ledger, A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 or A6 (any letter case). Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `format`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`format must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/pdf`)_
- `landscape` — Use landscape orientation. `true` or `false`; any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `landscape`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`landscape must not be repeated`).
- `printBackground` — Include background graphics. `true` or `false`; any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `printBackground`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`printBackground must not be repeated`).
- `margin` — Uniform margin: a non-negative number of pixels, or a number followed by `px`, `in`, `cm` or `mm` (e.g. '1cm', '0.5in'). Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `margin`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`margin must not be repeated`).
- `url` — Optional URL to navigate the tab to before reading it. Only an absolute `http`, `https` or `data` URL, `about:blank`, or (on Chromium engines only) a `chrome:` URL is accepted. Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, and so is a value that is not an absolute URL or an empty `url=` (omit `url` to read the current page). The `url` is checked before an instance is started, a tab is looked up, or anything is navigated. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/markdown`)_
- `onlyMainContent` — `true`: only the main content (Defuddle's extraction). `false`: the whole page body, after the same cleanup. `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `onlyMainContent`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`onlyMainContent must not be repeated`).
- `includeImages` — `false` removes images from the Markdown (embeds such as YouTube videos stay). `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `includeImages`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeImages must not be repeated`).
- `includeLinks` — `true` adds `links`: every `http`/`https` link on the page, resolved, without fragments, published like the Markdown's links, sorted and deduplicated, at most 10 000. `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `includeLinks`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeLinks must not be repeated`).
- `frontmatter` — `true` puts a YAML frontmatter block (`title`, `author`, `site`, `published`, `language`, `description`, `source`; empty keys left out) on top of the Markdown. The block is not counted against `maxChars`. `true` or `false`; omitted or empty uses the default. Any other value is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `frontmatter`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`frontmatter must not be repeated`).
- `maxChars` — Longest Markdown body returned, in characters. A longer one is cut at the last line break within the limit when there is one after the first character, otherwise at the limit without splitting a surrogate pair; `truncated` is then true. Any value outside 1 to 2000000 is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `maxChars`. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`maxChars must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/markdown`)_
- `instanceGeneration` — The instance generation from /metadata. If it no longer matches the running instance → 409 INSTANCE_CHANGED (also when no instance exists: details.expected is null). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`instanceGeneration must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot`)_
- `timeoutMs` — Budget for the whole browser operation, starting at handler entry (instance provisioning is never inside it). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`timeoutMs must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name does not suppress that: it is governed by the body schema instead. A body that is not a JSON object at all, or that fails the operation's own validation, is rejected first, with its own message and the same status and code. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot`)_
- `maxChars` — Hard cut on a line boundary; `truncated` reports it. A truncated excerpt may not parse as standalone YAML. Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`maxChars must not be repeated`). _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/snapshot`)_
- `includeValues` — Include the CONTENTS of form controls in the snapshot. Off by default: the accessibility tree serialises `input.value`, so a snapshot taken after the agent typed a password, card number or token would hand those back on every subsequent loop iteration. With the default, the value of a non-empty textbox, searchbox, spinbutton, slider or editable combobox (an input with a `<datalist>`, or `role=combobox`) renders as `<value hidden>`, whatever its label contains; only a native `<select>` keeps its option names, when it holds nothing but `<option>`, `<optgroup>` and `<hr>` elements and none of them uses `aria-owns` or `aria-labelledby` or is editable (every other node in it keeps its role and ref but not its name or text), and the content of every other combobox, ARIA autocomplete popups and customizable selects with rich option content included, is hidden whole (an empty one renders with no value at all, so the caller can still tell them apart). Content inside an editable region (a `contenteditable` element, or a whole page in `designMode`) is hidden too: the region keeps its role and ref, its contents become `<value hidden>`, and its name is shown only when it is authored (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at non-editable content); text the snapshot folds from an editor into an enclosing element is hidden there too. If the page cannot be asked in time, the text and computed names on such a page are hidden and the refs are kept. Set to `true` only when the values are known not to be sensitive. Omitted or empty uses the default (false); any other value than `true` or `false` is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, and repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`includeValues must not be repeated`).
- `waitUntil` — Navigation readiness to wait for. networkidle is deliberately not offered. Repeating this key IN THE QUERY STRING is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`waitUntil must not be repeated`), on GET and on POST alike: two copies could disagree about when the navigation is done and only the last would be read. The rule is about the query string only: a JSON body property named `waitUntil` is governed by the body schema, not by this.
- `timeoutMs` — Budget for viewport settling + navigation. Omitted: the navigation itself may take up to 30000 ms (the server bounds the request with `--request-timeout`). Present: the whole budget, and the server bounds the request by timeoutMs + 5 s. Either way a navigation that runs out of time is a `504 TIMEOUT` (phase navigation). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`timeoutMs must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name does not suppress that: it is governed by the body schema instead. A body that is not a JSON object at all, or that fails the operation's own validation, is rejected first, with its own message and the same status and code. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/browse`)_
- `instanceGeneration` — From /metadata; mismatch → 409 INSTANCE_CHANGED (also when no instance exists, and no instance is spawned). Repeating this key in the query string is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`instanceGeneration must not be repeated`); a body property of the same name is governed by the body schema. _(on `GET /api/v1/browser/browse`)_
- `active` — Make the tab active (focused) after navigation. Strict boolean: spell it `true` or `false` and nothing else. `1`, `0`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `TRUE`, and a present-but-empty `?active=` are each rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.field` names the parameter) before any tab is created or reused. A supplied value is never coerced and never silently falls back to the default. ONLY omitting the parameter takes the default. Repeating the key is not an error on this parameter: the instance reads the last occurrence. That leniency is specific to the `/browse` booleans. The server rejects a repeated QUERY key named `url`, `waitUntil`, `script`, `scriptBase64`, `tabId`, `instanceGeneration`, `maxChars`, `includeValues` or `timeoutMs` with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Those name a destination, a program or a bound, where two disagreeing copies must not resolve silently to one. That rule inspects the query string and nothing else: a JSON body property sharing one of those names, array-valued or not, is governed by the operation's body schema instead.
- `onlyIfNotExists` — Reuse an existing tab whose URL already equals the target instead of opening a new one. The reused tab is still navigated (this is tab reuse, not a navigation dedup). Same strict boolean rule as `active`: only `true` or `false`; anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.
- `ignoreGetParameters` — Ignore query parameters when checking for existing URL. Same strict boolean rule as `active`: only `true` or `false`; anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.

**Body shapes:**

- `POST /api/v1/browser/action` body — `{ instanceGeneration: string, tabId: int, timeoutMs: int=10000, action*: "click" | "fill" | "type" | "press" | "select" | "check" | "hover", target*: browser_Target, dialog: browser_DialogPolicy, value: string, delayMs: int=0, key: string, values: string[], checked: bool, button: "left" | "middle" | "right"="left", clickCount: int=1, modifiers: ("Alt" | "Control" | "Meta" | "Shift")[] }`
  - `instanceGeneration` — From /metadata; mismatch → 409 INSTANCE_CHANGED.
  - `tabId` — Tab to act on (from /tabs); omitted → active tab; unknown → 404 TAB_NOT_FOUND.
  - `timeoutMs` — Budget for the whole browser operation (body overrides query).
  - `value` — fill / type: the text. Never echoed.
  - `delayMs` — type: delay between keys. Code points × delayMs must be smaller than timeoutMs (400).
  - `key` — press: Playwright key syntax (e.g. "Enter", "Control+a"). Unknown → 400.
  - `values` — select: option values or labels (first match wins). No match → 504 with details.availableOptions.
  - `checked` — check: desired state (idempotent).
- `POST /api/v1/browser/eval` body — `{ script: string, tabId: int, scriptBase64: bool, timeoutMs: int=30000 }` — Executes a JavaScript snippet provided in the request body. …
  - `script` — JavaScript code to execute
  - `tabId` — Tab to evaluate in (from `/tabs`). Omitted: the active tab. Unknown → `404 TAB_NOT_FOUND`, malformed → `400`.
  - `scriptBase64` — Set to `true` when `script` is base64-encoded.
- `POST /api/v1/browser/browse` body — `{ url*: string, tabId: int, waitUntil: "commit" | "domcontentloaded" | "load"="load", timeoutMs: int, instanceGeneration: string, active: bool=true, onlyIfNotExists: bool=false, ignoreGetParameters: bool=false }`
  - `url` — … Any other scheme (`file:` in any spelling unless the kit was started with local-file access enabled, `view-source:`, `javascript:`, `blob:` and the rest) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an http, https or data URL, about:blank, or a chrome URL on Chromium; file and other local schemes are refused`), and a value that is not an absolute URL (such as `/etc/hostname`) is a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`url must be an absolute URL, like https://example.com/`). …
  - `timeoutMs` — Omitted: the navigation may take up to 30000 ms. Present: the whole budget. Either way a navigation that runs out of time is a 504 TIMEOUT (phase navigation).
  - `active` — Whether the tab becomes the active one. … ANY other value (`0`, `1`, `"yes"`, `"on"`, `""`, `null`, or an array) is rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.field` names the property) before a tab is created or reused; it is never coerced. …
  - `onlyIfNotExists` — Reuse an existing tab already on this URL instead of opening a new one. Same value rule as `active`: send a JSON boolean (the strings `"true"`/`"false"` are tolerated because one parser reads both the query and the body spelling); anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.
  - `ignoreGetParameters` — Compare URLs for `onlyIfNotExists` with the query string stripped. Same value rule as `active`: send a JSON boolean (the strings `"true"`/`"false"` are tolerated because one parser reads both the query and the body spelling); anything else is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, never coerced.
- `POST /api/v1/browser/wait` body — `{ instanceGeneration: string, tabId: int, timeoutMs: int=10000, condition*: browser_WaitCondition }`

### `tabs` (2) — Browser tab lifecycle

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `POST /api/v1/browser/tab/close` | Close a browser tab | `?browser_id` `?start` `body` |
| `GET /api/v1/browser/tabs` | List browser tabs | `?browser_id` `?start` |

**Body shapes:**

- `POST /api/v1/browser/tab/close` body — `{ tabId: int }`
  - `tabId` — The ID of the tab to close

### `viewport` (2) — Runtime viewport policy of a running instance

| Method | Summary | Params |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/v1/browser/viewport` | Get the current viewport policy | `?browser_host` `?browser_port` |
| `POST /api/v1/browser/viewport` | Change the viewport at runtime | `?browser_host` `?browser_port` `body*` |

**Param notes:**

- `browser_host` — Instance host. Optional. Must be paired with browser_port; when both are omitted the single running instance is selected (400 AMBIGUOUS_INSTANCE with more than one).
- `browser_port` — Instance port. Optional. Must be paired with browser_host.

**Body shapes:**

- `POST /api/v1/browser/viewport` body — `{ viewport*: { width*: int, height*: int }|null }`
  - `viewport` — Fixed size {width,height} (integers 1..8192, no other keys), or null for responsive.


### Body schemas

- `browser_Target` — `{ ref: string, snapshotId: string, selector: string, role: string, name: string, label: string, text: string, placeholder: string, testId: string, exact: bool=true }`
  - … Exactly ONE of ref, selector, role, label, text, placeholder, testId must be set (400 otherwise). `name` only with role; `snapshotId` required with ref; `exact` only with role/label/text/placeholder (default true). Every target is strict: more than one match → 409 AMBIGUOUS_TARGET. …
  - `ref` — Element reference from the latest /snapshot of this tab (e.g. "e12"). Requires snapshotId.
  - `snapshotId` — The snapshotId the ref came from. Must be the tab's latest and no main-frame navigation may have happened since (409 STALE_SNAPSHOT otherwise).
  - `selector` — A single CSS selector (forced through Playwright's css engine; ">>" chaining and other engines are rejected with 400).
  - `role` — ARIA role (Playwright's closed role list; unknown → 400). Combine with name.
  - `name` — Accessible name, only with role.
- `browser_DialogPolicy` — `{ type*: "alert" | "confirm" | "prompt" | "beforeunload", response*: "accept" | "dismiss", promptText: string, message: string }`
  - Authorizes handling of ONE dialog raised during this action; it never requires one (no dialog → `dialog: null`). A dialog that does not match, or a second dialog, is dismissed and the action fails with 409 UNEXPECTED_DIALOG (details.outcome says whether the mutation had completed).
  - `message` — If set, the dialog's message must equal this exactly to be handled.
- `browser_WaitCondition` — `{ kind*: "target" | "text" | "url" | "loadState", target: browser_Target, state: "attached" | "detached" | "visible" | "hidden" | "enabled" | "disabled" | "domcontentloaded" | "load", text: string, match: "contains" | "equals"="contains", url: string, urlPrefix: string }`
  - Discriminated by `kind`. target: {target, state}; text: {target, text, match?}; url: exactly one of {url} (absolute, compared as normalized href) or {urlPrefix} (verbatim startsWith on href); loadState: {state}. A miss is 504 TIMEOUT (phase wait), never matched:false.

---

<!-- ===== namespace: code ===== -->

# `code` — VS Code in the browser, per computer

## Purpose

**This is the VS Code IDE running in a browser tab — not a programmatic API.** Open `https://{P}-{C}-code-1.{N}.computers.hoody.com/` and you get the full editor: file tree, diff view, debugger, terminals, extensions marketplace, all backed by the computer's filesystem. The `code-N` URL is served by an **orchestrator** that starts one isolated editor instance per index and returns a page that embeds it. The index is the hostname: `code-1` is instance 1, `code-2` is instance 2, each with its own settings, state and running process.

On a `code-N` host the platform's edge fills in the two parameters the entry page needs. It sets the instance selector `id` from the hostname, overwriting anything the caller sent, and it sets `folder` to the computer's default workspace when the request names none. Add `?folder=<abs-path>` to open a different folder. Talking to a bare kit server with no edge in front of it, a client must send both `folder` and `id` itself: with neither the entry path returns the kit specification, with only one it returns `400`.

The methods in this namespace read the service's state (health, running instances, versions), stop editor instances, stage extensions and confirm what an instance has installed, and build embed URLs. Day-to-day use is "open the URL".

Like every Hoody kit URL, `code` is **iframable**: drop the `code-N` URL into an `<iframe>` and you've embedded VS Code in your own page. Same for every other kit UI (`files`, `terminal`, `display`, `desktop`, `browser`, `notes`, `agent`, …), except that an `exec` script's response keeps the framing policy it sends — you can compose a full HTML "operating system" out of Hoody kit iframes with no native code, just URLs and standard CSP / cookie wiring.

**Headline mode: extension-only embed.** Add `?extension=<publisher>.<name>` and the editor hides its chrome and opens that extension's **sidebar view** filling the viewport. It works for an installed extension that contributes a sidebar view (an Activity Bar panel); when no sidebar view of that extension can be found, even after activating it, the editor falls back to the file explorer. Pair such an extension with the iframable kit URL and you have:

- A coding agent (e.g. **Cline** — `saoudrizwan.claude-dev`) accessible from any browser, including mobile phones with no IDE installed.
- The same agent embedded into your own dashboard, a docs site, a Notion page, a Slack canvas (URL preview), a CRM, or any other HTML surface.
- A focused tool surface from any other extension with its own sidebar view (Continue, Roo Cline, GitLens, …) without exposing the full editor. An extension that only adds editors, commands or previews has no sidebar view to open.
- A branded deployment: point a proxy alias at the `code` service and hand out the alias URL instead of one that carries the `computerId` (Example 7). The embedded editor can still reveal the computer identifiers in the page's HTML; the alias brands the link, it does not hide the computer.

The computer's filesystem still backs the extension (it can edit files, run terminals, hit the network, etc.) — same persistent state as the full IDE. To run two single-extension surfaces side by side, give each its own instance through its own hostname: Cline on `code-1`, Continue on `code-2`.

## When to use

- **Humans editing code**: hand the user the URL — that's the whole product.
- **Single-extension embed for an agent or tool** — `?extension=<publisher>.<name>` opens that extension's sidebar view full-screen; iframable, mobile-friendly, distributable behind a proxy alias.
- Pre-open a folder with `?folder=<abs-path>`, so the URL is bookmarkable.
- Stage a custom VSIX with `POST /api/v1/code/extensions/install`, then confirm with `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` that an instance actually installed it.
- Read which editor instances are running (`GET /status`) and which orchestrator and editor builds are deployed (`GET /api/v1/code/version`).

## When NOT to use

Not for: non-interactive shell → `terminal`/`exec`, file I/O without a UI → `files`, long-lived processes → `daemon`, headless web → `browser`, exposing a dev server that runs in the computer → a proxy alias with program `http` and its port (see the `api` namespace). Not a coding-agent control plane → `agent` (the typed in-computer AI-agent HTTP namespace, slug `agent`; the Hoody Agent browser GUI on the same `-agent-1` host is the human surface).

## Prerequisites

- A running computer. Set `P`, `C`, `N` (project id, computer id, server name) from `GET /api/v1/computers/{id}`.
- Address the service through its `code-N` URL. That hostname selects the instance. 
- VSIX staging needs a downloadable `.vsix` URL that the service may fetch: `http` or `https`, no credentials in the URL, and not an address inside the computer or on a private network.

## Capability URL

→ See `SKILL-HTTP.md § Proxy URLs`.

**Reaching a service you host on a computer port** (any port, any namespace):

- `https://{projectId}-{computerId}-http-<port>.{node}.computers.hoody.com` — proxy speaks HTTP to `<port>` on the computer's network address. Bind `0.0.0.0:<port>`, which always works; a loopback-only listener is also reached on default computers.
- `https://{projectId}-{computerId}-https-<port>.{node}.computers.hoody.com` — proxy speaks HTTPS to `<port>` on the computer's network address (target needs TLS, bound to `0.0.0.0:<port>` too).

Edge is always `https://`. No alias, firewall edit, or proxy registration needed; capability-token gates still apply.

## Common workflows

### 1. Open the editor on a folder

1. Open `https://{P}-{C}-code-1.{N}.computers.hoody.com/?folder=<abs-path>`. Leave `folder` out to open the computer's default workspace.
2. To switch folders, open the same URL with another `folder`. A running instance is reused, and the page loads the editor on the folder the request names. `GET /status` keeps reporting the folder the instance was started with. Add `restart=true` only when you mean to restart the instance's process.

### 2. Embed a single extension (single-tool browser surface)

1. Make sure the extension is installed in that instance: stage it (workflow 3) or install it in the editor.
2. Open or iframe `https://{P}-{C}-code-1.{N}.computers.hoody.com/?extension=<publisher>.<name>&folder=<abs-path>`.
3. Brand it with `POST /api/v1/proxy/aliases` (program `code`, the landing query in `target_path`) and gate it with `* /api/v1/computers/{id}/proxy/permissions*` before sharing.

### 3. Stage a VSIX, apply it, confirm it installed

1. `POST /api/v1/code/extensions/install` with the `.vsix` URL. A success means the file is staged, not installed: the response reports `requiresRestartToApply: true` and `appliesAt: "next-instance-start"`. 
2. Start or restart the instance that should have it (open its URL with `restart=true`). Staging is shared across instances, so every instance attempts to install it at its next start.
3. `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` and read `observed`: to confirm installation at the staged version, require `status: "running"`, a non-null `stagedVersion` and `installedVersion === stagedVersion` (an installed extension with nothing staged also reports `running`). This compares version numbers only; it does not show that the extension activated.

### 4. Inspect instances and versions

1. `GET /status` lists the running instances (id, port, folder, uptime) and the orchestrator's `basePort`.
2. `GET /api/v1/code/version` reports the orchestrator build and the packaged editor tree separately.

### 5. Stop an editor instance and release capacity

Stop an instance you no longer need: it ends its editors, integrated terminals, tasks and extension host, and keeps its settings, installed extensions and workspace state for its next start.

Send `DELETE /api/v1/code` to that instance's `code-<id>` URL (`<id>` is the instance index, `1` for the first editor).

A `200` means the instance was stopped, or its start was cancelled before a process existed; any process it had has exited. `404` with `unknown-instance` means there was nothing to stop.

## Quirks & gotchas

- On a `code-N` host the edge sets `id` from the hostname and overwrites a caller's value, so a query-string `id` cannot pick another instance. `code-0` is treated as `code-1`.
- The edge fills `folder` with the computer's default workspace only when the request carries no `folder`; an explicit `folder` wins.
- A request with a different `folder` for a running instance reuses that instance and its page loads the editor on the requested folder; no restart is needed. The instance keeps the folder it was started with as its own, which is the one `GET /status` reports. `restart=true` kills and respawns the instance.
- The entry path forwards only the query parameters it declares (`?folder`, `?id`, `?extension`, `?restart`, `?page-loader`, `?disable-walkthroughs`, `?hoody-code`, `?welcome-iframe-url`, `?page-loader-path`, `?proxy-domain`, `?locale`, `?app-name`) and drops any other name without reporting it.
- The query string on the entry path is capped at 8192 bytes; a longer one is answered `400` and starts nothing.
- The page embeds the editor from a separate host of the computer. That host is editor transport, not part of the kit API: use the `code-N` URL.
- Staging is not installation. The editor installs staged extensions only while an instance starts, and the stage directory is shared, so one stage reaches every instance at its next start.
- A stage that lands while an instance is starting can be installed with one version's details and another's contents. `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` reads only the installed version number, so it may not reveal that pairing; restarting the instance installs whatever is staged then. Stage before starting an instance.
- `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` keeps `desired` (what is staged) and `observed` (what this instance appears to have) apart. A section that could not be read reports `status: "unavailable"` and has no `extensions` key at all, and `partial` is then true.
- An observed entry's `status` is `running` (the instance is running and its installed version equals the staged version, or the extension is installed with nothing staged for it), `stale` (normal between a stage and the next start), `failed` (started after the stage and still lacks it), `stopped` or `unavailable`. `running` is a version comparison, not proof that the extension activated. Match entries on `logicalKey`, the lowercased `publisher.name`.
- `allowDowngrade` is off by default, so a restage cannot silently roll an extension back; a refused downgrade is `409`.
- `GET /api/v1/code/version` reports the orchestrator and the packaged editor as two figures because they are built and deployed separately. It never contacts the network and there is no update check.
- `GET /api/v1/code/health`, `GET /status` and `GET /api/v1/code/version` take no query parameters; an `id` sent to them changes nothing.
- Building an extension-only URL does not open the editor or start an instance. Compose it from the `code-N` URL with the `extension` and `folder` query parameters. 
- `kit_slug` always `code`.

## Common errors

- `429` HTML page from the entry path — starting another instance would pass the instance limit this deployment is configured with (none by default). Nothing was started; stop an instance you do not need (workflow 5), then retry. An already running instance is still served at the limit.
- `403` — Refused by the Source IP Guard: Hoody Kit programs are reached through their URLs only. The body is the plain text `Forbidden`, not JSON. Use the `code-N` URL.
- `400` HTML page from the entry path: exactly one of `folder` and `id` carried a value, `id` is not an unsigned decimal integer or was sent twice, `id` exceeds `65535 - basePort`, or the query is over 8192 bytes. On a `code-N` host the edge fills `id`, and fills the default `folder` only when the `folder` key is absent, so an explicit empty `?folder=` still gets this `400`.
- `409` from the entry path: the instance's port is held by a process the orchestrator did not start. Retrying does not help until it is released.
- `503` from the entry path: the instance failed to start, was cancelled or did not become ready in time, exited or stopped before it was ready, or the orchestrator is shutting down. Worth retrying once the condition clears.
- `POST /api/v1/code/extensions/install` errors carry a stable `error` code: `destination-refused` (`403`, the URL is outside the fetch policy), `downgrade-refused` (`409`), `not-a-vsix` (`422`), `upstream-error` (`502`, may be retried), `upstream-timeout` (`504`), `installs-at-capacity` (`503`, honour `Retry-After`), `insufficient-storage` (`507`), `extension-too-large` (`413`, the archive is over the size limit). Branch on `error`, not on the message.
- Either extensions operation can return `invalid-selector` (`400`, an `id` the service cannot parse) or `internal-error` (`500`). Only `POST /api/v1/code/extensions/install` reads a request body, so only it returns `invalid-request` (`400`, malformed body or `url`), `unsupported-media-type` (`415`, body not sent as `application/json`) and `request-too-large` (`413`, body over the limit).
- `404` with `error: "unknown-instance"` from either extensions operation means the service has no extensions directory configured, despite the code's name; retrying with another instance id does not help. An instance that was never started lists as `stopped`, not 404.
- `503` from `GET /api/v1/code/extensions/list` carries the normal result body with `desired.status: "unavailable"`: the staged set could not be read, and `observed` is still reported.

## Related namespaces

→ `terminal`, `files`, `exec`, `browser`, `daemon`, `api` (proxy aliases and permissions).

## Examples

`code` is a **URL-first** namespace — for most workflows the kit URL itself (with the right query string and / or iframe wrapper) IS the deliverable. The methods here read state, stage extensions and build URLs; they do not drive the editor. Each example below is a copy-pasteable recipe in the mode you're reading. URL-composition steps are pure string templates and need no kit call. Set `P`, `C`, `N` (project id, computer id, server name) from `GET /api/v1/computers/{id}` first.

### 1. Open the editor with a folder pre-loaded — bookmarkable URL

**Goal:** ship a teammate a single URL that opens VS Code already pointing at the right repo.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-code-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com"
URL="$KIT/?folder=/home/user/myrepo"
echo "$URL"
# The edge sets id=1 from the code-1 hostname. Leave ?folder out to open the
# computer's default workspace instead.
```

### 2. Extension-only embed — open one extension's sidebar view

**Goal:** open `code-1` as a single extension's panel — the editor chrome is hidden and the extension's sidebar view fills the viewport. Pair it with a folder so the extension opens with the right repo selected. The extension must be installed in that instance and contribute a sidebar view; otherwise the file explorer opens instead.

URL pattern (no kit call):

```
https://${P}-${C}-code-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com/?extension=<publisher>.<name>&folder=<absolute-path>
```

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-code-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com"
URL="$KIT/?extension=saoudrizwan.claude-dev&folder=/home/user/myrepo"
echo "$URL"
```

Name the extension as `publisher.name`, no version. The entry page forwards the value as sent; the editor also accepts a sidebar view container id such as `workbench.view.scm`, or part of one. A second surface (say Continue, `continue.continue`) goes on its own instance: build the same URL on `code-2`.

### 3. Open another folder on a running instance

**Goal:** instance 1 is open on `/home/user/myrepo` and you want the editor on `/home/user/other`. Open the same instance URL with the new `folder`: the running instance is reused and the page loads the editor on that folder. `GET /status` keeps reporting the folder the instance was started with.

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-code-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com"
URL="$KIT/?folder=/home/user/other"
echo "$URL"   # open it in the browser; no restart needed
```

Add `restart=true` only when the process itself must restart, for example to apply a staged extension (Example 4). Restarting ends that instance's running editor session, including its terminals. Other instances are untouched.

### 4. Stage a custom VSIX and confirm it installed

**Goal:** push an internal extension (`.vsix`) into the editor and confirm the instance has it installed.

**Step 1 — stage it.**

```bash
KIT="https://${P}-${C}-code-1.${N}.computers.hoody.com"
```
